extracted.intended_audience: secondary-school students studying North Carolina history / pupils using a 19th-century state history textbook
extracted.subtask_description: A set of chapter-end reading-comprehension prompts and factual questions intended to test students' recall, understanding, and synthesis of the historical chapters on North Carolina's post-war society, industry, transport, literature, and education. Used by teachers to guide lessons and assess comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war expectations and obstacles (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what period had the people of North Carolina been looking forward since the close of the war? What acts had somewhat prevented the arrival of this state of affairs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehension question assessing students' grasp of the anticipated post-war state and specific events or acts that delayed that condition. Context: closing of the Civil War and Reconstruction-era impediments (preceding chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political animosities and prosperity (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of political animosities and the general prosperity of the State? Of towns and factories?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates ability to summarize statements about partisan conflict and economic recovery, including urban and industrial development described in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masonic charitable institution (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What charitable institution had been opened by the Masons? Who was put in charge?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of institutions established and their leadership as examples of post-war civic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orphan Asylum (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the Orphan Asylum?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests recall of details about specific charitable institutions mentioned in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: University and other colleges' condition (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: In what condition was the University? What is said of other colleges?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses understanding of higher education's state and recovery after political interference and reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Female school mentioned (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What female school is now mentioned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple factual recall about educational institutions for women referenced in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political changes in 1872 Presidential campaign (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What political changes were seen in the Presidential campaign of 1872?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates comprehension of shifting political alliances and voter behavior described for 1872.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation for political course (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What was said to have dictated this course? What was the general position of the people since the close of the war?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks students to cite reasons given in the text for political decisions and the population's overall stance postwar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of continuing sectional prejudices (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the cause of sectional prejudices continuing to exist?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks ability to explain factors the author assigns for lingering sectional animosities.

rubrics_metrics.name: American characteristics and removal of animosities (Ch. before LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: In what characteristics do the American people stand high? Why should all sectional animosities be speedily removed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses interpretation of the author's argument about national character and the imperative for reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flax cultivation before the cotton gin (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What was a principle crop in North Carolina before the cotton gin was invented? What is said of the cultivation of flax?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall about pre-gin agriculture and the role of flax for household use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift from flax to cotton (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why did the production of cotton so rapidly take the place of flax?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests understanding of economic and technological reasons (cotton gin, comparative competitiveness) for crop substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment of people's means pre-war (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: How did the people invest nearly all their means?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of the text's point that capital was invested largely in slaves and cotton plantations rather than industrial enterprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cotton factories description (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What can you tell of the various cotton factories?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses ability to summarize the growth, employment scale, and economic effects of cotton mills in the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barriers to entering manufacturing (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why have not our people entered more largely into this class of industry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires explanation of cultural/investment hesitations and historical reasons impeding manufacturing development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future prosperity yet to be attained (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What better future prosperity is yet to be attained by the State?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates comprehension of the author's vision for industrialization and transportation improvements needed for full prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tobacco industry importance (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What other great industry is now considered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recognition that tobacco processing and market development are highlighted as the State's other major industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tobacco production in North Carolina (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What had been the production in North Carolina?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall about historical tobacco volumes and quality potential discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tobacco peddlers (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the tobacco peddlers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses understanding of small-scale peddling practices and the impact of internal revenue laws on itinerant sellers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment animating the people (Ch. LXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: What sentiment animates the people of North Carolina?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates comprehension of the concluding sentiment praising industry creators and town founders as public benefactors.

rubrics_metrics.name: State excitement in 1876 (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the State excited in 1876?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests recall that the excitement was over the choice of new men for Chief-Magistrates (national and state elections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Result of 1876 gubernatorial election (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the result of this election?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual: requires naming Z. B. Vance's choice over Judge Thomas Settle and understanding the election's significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events of the past few years (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the events of the past few years?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks students to summarize recent political and social changes (e.g., end of Reconstruction federal troops, return to local control) described in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural benefits from new methods (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: How have the agricultural pursuits of the State been benefited?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses understanding of fertilizer use, improved cultivation, and educated planters engaging directly in management leading to increased cotton yields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important employments and commercial advantages (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the most important employments in a State? What are some of North Carolina's commercial advantages?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates grasp of the centrality of agriculture and commerce and the limitations/opportunities from ports, railways, and natural resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial condition at war's end (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the financial condition of the people at the close of the war?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of merchant and bank ruin and general impoverishment of debtors postwar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raleigh as trade centre (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of Raleigh as a trade centre?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks for description of Raleigh's modest commercial standing historically and its later expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade improvement at the capital (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: In what way did trade matters begin to improve at the capital?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests recognition of influx of energetic young men, railway expansion, and entrepreneurial activity that expanded Raleigh's trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: North Carolina's commercial prospects and Cotton Exchange (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What else is said of North Carolina's commercial prospects? What advantage has Raleigh derived from the Cotton Exchange?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses understanding of anticipated manufacturing growth and the role of the Cotton Exchange in increasing cotton sales and trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Israelites' contribution (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the Israelites?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall that Jewish citizens in towns contributed to trade and have synagogues in several cities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fish hatchery enterprise (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What new enterprise was inaugurated in 1878? What have been the results of the hatchery? What fact has been proven concerning fish?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall and explanation about the state-run fish hatchery, its stocking results, and spawning/return migration facts demonstrated by naturalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement in catching fish (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the improvement in the means of catching fish?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses understanding of steam-powered seines, Dutch Nets, ice, and rapid transport enabling broader fish markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eastern counties' trade species (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What other species of trade is found in the eastern counties?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of vegetable growing (Irish potatoes, peas) and multiple cropping on alluvial soils supplying distant markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of peanuts (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the production of peanuts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests recall of the recent extension of peanut cultivation and its growing economic importance in eastern counties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth and trade of Wilmington (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you tell something of the growth and trade of Wilmington?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates comprehension of Wilmington's expanded foreign visits, steam packet lines, and commercial revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigation improvements of Cape Fear River (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: How has the navigation of the Cape Fear River been improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of federal appropriations, closing of New Inlet, and stone barrier works improving river approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other seaport city and its commercial interests (Ch. LXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What other seaport city is now mentioned? What is said of its commercial interests?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall about New Bern's shipping point development, freight lines, and trade in lumber and produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railroad extension and map identification (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the subject of this lesson? What is said of the extension of the Raleigh & Gaston Railroad? Go to the map and point out this road.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests ability to state the chapter's topic (railroads and new towns), summarize Raleigh & Gaston extension to Weldon, and locate it on a map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favored trunk-line and Civil War importance (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What favorite trunk-line has long been desired? What road was specially important to the Confederate government? Point out this road on the map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses recognition of proposed east-west trunk line to Beaufort, and the line to Petersburg tapped during the war; map skills implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recently completed roads (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What roads are mentioned as having been recently completed? Point out these on the map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of specific railroad lines listed (Charlotte-Wilmington, Charlotte-Statesville, Raleigh-Hamlet, Cape Fear & Yadkin Valley, Western NC Road, Paint Rock branch, etc.) and ability to map them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Towns and their growth (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What towns are now mentioned, and what is said of their growth? Locate them on the map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses comprehension of rapid town growth (Winston, Durham, Reidsville, Charlotte, Salisbury, Greensboro) and geographic location skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosperity of Charlotte (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the prosperity of the city of Charlotte?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests recall and summary of Charlotte's enterprise, trade, railway importance, and rise to prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centennial at Charlotte (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the centennial celebration at Charlotte? When did it occur?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall of the Mecklenburg Declaration centennial event on May 20th, 1875, and its attendees and speeches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fayetteville, Asheville, Statesville mentions (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What mention is made of Fayetteville, Asheville and Statesville? Find these towns on the map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses ability to summarize their thrift and expansion and to locate them geographically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of rapid town growth (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What have been the causes of the rapid growth of the towns in the state?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates understanding of railroad erection, manufactories, immigrants, and resource exploitation as causal factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further prosperity noticed (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What further prosperity is noticed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks comprehension of continued commercial expansion, railway reach into mountains, and exploitation of mineral and agricultural products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Western medicinal root industry (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What other industry is described? Can you tell anything of this valuable production? (Teacher will explain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompts recall and teacher-led discussion about ginseng and medicinal root collection and processing in western counties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Western fruit growers (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the western fruit growers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses recall of frost-free elevations, orchard development, and apple shipments from western counties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native grape varieties (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What excellent varieties of grape are natives of North Carolina? What is said of the Catawba grape?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall about Scuppernong and Catawba grapes and their value to nurseries and cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacture of stronger liquors (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What mention is made of the manufacture of stronger liquors?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks understanding of distilleries, 'Moonshiners,' federal regulation, and enforcement conflicts discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death of State officer (Ch. LXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What State officer died at this period? What is said of Major Engelhard?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall regarding the death of Secretary of State Joseph A. Engelhard and his public service and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson subject on literature (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of what does this lesson treat?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple identification of the chapter's topic: literature and authors of North Carolina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sir Walter Raleigh and literary tendencies (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who is the first literary man known to North Carolina? What is said of him? What others are mentioned in this connection?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses recall of Sir Walter Raleigh's connection and early literary figures like Hariot, Lawson, and Dr. Brickell.

rubrics_metrics.name: General literary condition of the State (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What has been the general condition of literary matters in the State? Why have so few professional authors been seen?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests ability to explain the author's view that while there were cultivated individuals, the mass had little book knowledge depressing professional authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samuel Swann and Edward Moseley (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of Samuel Swan and Edward Moseley? Who was author of the 'Atticus Letter?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires naming prominent pre-Revolutionary literary/legal figures and identifying Judge Maurice Moore as author of the 'Atticus Letter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of 'Atticus Letter' and literary men of that period (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What mention is made of the 'Atticus Letter?' Who were the literary men of that period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks comprehension of that literary controversy and names of lawyers and writers active then.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence and Iredell's efforts (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the correspondence of that day? What was the extent of Judge Iredell's literary efforts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses recall of extensive polite correspondence and Iredell's law book and newspaper dissertations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attainments of Dr. Hugh Williamson (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the attainments of Dr. Hugh Williamson?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual recall about Williamson's roles as physician, professor, congressman, and historian with moderate success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other historians and their mention (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What other historians are mentioned, and what is said of them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recognition of Judge Francois Xavier Martin and his valuable compilations and histories, with few errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labors of Joseph Seawell Jones (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell something of the labors of Joseph Seawell Jones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates recall of Jones's social prominence, literary works (Defense of Revolutionary History), and later life on a Mississippi plantation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement in literary affairs early in the century (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What produced an improvement in literary affairs early in the present century?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses understanding that students of Dr. Joseph Caldwell and practical, scientific instruction improved literary aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ode to Carolina and gifted writers (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the ode to Carolina and its author? What writers of similar gifts are named? What is said of musical compositions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of Judge William Gaston's ode, other poetic writers, and limited musical composition production aside from two favored songs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efforts of Colonel Wheeler and Dr. Wiley (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the literary efforts of Colonel Wheeler and Dr Wiley? What other historical writers are mentioned who have contributed to the State valuable series of school books?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests recall of their historical contributions and names of educators/professors who produced school textbooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawyers' legal works (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What members of the Bar have produced legal works of great value?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates recollection of named lawyers (Iredell, Cantwell, Swam, Eaton, Moore, Olds, Battle, Busbee, etc.) and the nature of their legal digests and manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifted women writers (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you tell something of the gifted women of the State?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks recall of named women authors (Spencer, Harris, Mary Mason, Mary Bayard Clarke, Frances Fisher a.k.a. 'Christian Reid') and their contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent newspaper editors (Ch. LXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: What prominent editors has the State furnished?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses recall of influential editors listed (Joseph Gales family, Edward J. Hale, W. W. Holden, Engelhard, Yates, P. M. Hale, Saunders, Ashe, etc.) and their impact.
